title: Seven bridges, one walk?
hook: A city of rivers and bridges. Is there a walk that crosses each bridge just once?

doesNotKnow: that a walk crossing every bridge once needs at most two places with an odd number of bridges

misconception: If I try hard enough, or start in the right place, I can find a route crossing every bridge once.
objective: The learner can explain that passing through a place uses two bridges, so only the start and end of a walk can have an odd bridge count; Königsberg has four odd places, so no such walk exists.

claims.text: In Euler's Königsberg problem there were 4 land areas joined by 7 bridges: the island to the north bank twice, to the south bank twice and to the east once, plus north-east and south-east.
claims.source: Euler, 'Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis' (1736). The stage map is a simplified diagram with the same connections, not to scale; the modern city (Kaliningrad) is not claimed.

claims.text: The bridge counts at the four places are 5, 3, 3 and 3: all four are odd.
claims.source: Island: 2 + 2 + 1 = 5; north: 2 + 1 = 3; south: 2 + 1 = 3; east: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Sum 14 = 2 × 7. degree() in Demo.tsx counts from the bridge list.

claims.text: Passing through a place uses two bridges, one in and one out, so only the start and the end of a walk can have an odd count; with more than two odd places no walk crosses every bridge exactly once, from any start.
claims.source: Euler (1736); for a connected graph a walk using every edge once exists iff 0 or 2 vertices have odd degree (Euler; sufficiency Hierholzer 1873).

claims.text: With bridge 7 (south-east) closed only two places are odd, and a walk crossing all six bridges exists.
claims.source: Counts become 5, 3, 2, 2 (island and north odd). Example walk: north-island-north-east-island-south-island (bridges 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), checked by hand and by the stage.

recall.question: A park has paths meeting at junctions; four junctions have 3 paths each and the rest have 2 or 4. Can you walk every path exactly once?
options: Yes, if you pick the right start
Only if the park is small
recall.why: Every junction you pass through uses two paths. Only the start and end can have an odd count, so four odd junctions are two too many.
